Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
700 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast:
A non-tropical, gale-force low pressure area centered a few hundred 
miles east of the North Carolina coast is producing disorganized 
showers and thunderstorms. This low is forecast to move northward 
into unfavorable environmental conditions, and development into a 
tropical or subtropical system is not expected.

Regardless of the system's status, this large weather system is 
still expected to produce heavy rains, gusty winds, dangerous surf, 
rip currents, and coastal flooding along portions of the eastern 
U.S. coasts during the next couple of days.  Additional information 
on this system, including Gale Warnings, can be found in High Seas 
Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, as well as 
products issued by your local National Weather Service forecast 
office.

* Formation chance through 7 days...low...near 0 percent.
